title: Fixed Deposit (FD)
description: A secure investment offered by banks where you deposit money for a fixed tenure at a guaranteed interest rate.
lockIn: 7 days to 10 years (penalty on early withdrawal)
liquidity: Moderate (can be prematurely closed with a minor interest penalty)
educationalSummary: Fixed Deposits are ideal for conservative investors seeking capital preservation and guaranteed returns. Interest earned is fully taxable as per your income tax slab, making them less tax-efficient for high-income earners but highly secure.
eligibility: All citizens, minors, HUFs, and NRI clients

title: Recurring Deposit (RD)
description: An investment tool allowing individuals to make regular monthly deposits and earn a fixed interest rate over a set period.
liquidity: Moderate (withdrawable before maturity with minor interest deduction)
educationalSummary: Recurring Deposits help individuals build a disciplined savings habit by investing a fixed sum monthly. Similar to FDs, the returns are guaranteed and highly secure, but the interest income is subject to TDS and taxes.

title: High-Yield Savings Account
description: A basic deposit account held at a retail bank that pays a modest interest rate and offers instant access to funds.
liquidity: Very High (instant access via ATM, UPI, net banking)
educationalSummary: A savings account is the most liquid place to park your emergency fund (typically 3-6 months of expenses). While interest rates are generally lower than FDs, up to ₹10,000 of savings account interest is tax-exempt under Section 80TTA.

title: Public Provident Fund (PPF)
description: A popular long-term government-backed savings scheme that offers attractive guaranteed interest rates and excellent tax benefits.
educationalSummary: PPF is one of the most powerful tax-saving tools because it follows the Exempt-Exempt-Exempt (EEE) status. The annual contribution (up to ₹1.5 lakh) is tax-deductible under 80C, the interest accumulated is tax-free, and the final maturity amount is completely tax-free.
eligibility: Resident Indian citizens (one account per individual; no HUF or NRI allowed)

title: Employees' Provident Fund (EPF)
description: A mandatory retirement benefits scheme for salaried employees, co-funded by the employee and employer.
lockIn: Until retirement or resignation (advances allowed for specific life events)
liquidity: Low (restricted to retirement or long-term unemployment)
educationalSummary: EPF provides automatic retirement savings with contributions deducted directly from your salary. It enjoys high interest rates compared to traditional savings accounts, tax deduction on employee contributions under 80C, and tax-exempt withdrawals on retirement.
eligibility: Salaried employees in organizations with 20+ workers

title: Post Office Savings Account
description: A highly secure deposit scheme offered by India Post branches, providing basic banking facilities to urban and rural populations.
liquidity: High (can withdraw at any Post Office branch)
educationalSummary: Post Office Savings Accounts offer unmatched reach and complete sovereign backing. It works like a traditional bank savings account with a fixed interest rate, and the interest received up to ₹3,500 (individual) / ₹7,000 (joint) is completely tax-exempt under Section 10(15).
eligibility: All individual Indian residents, including minors

title: Systematic Investment Plan (SIP)
description: A method of investing a fixed sum of money regularly in mutual funds, leveraging rupee cost averaging.
lockIn: None (unless investing in tax-saving ELSS funds which have 3 years lock-in)
educationalSummary: SIP is a disciplined investment methodology rather than a separate asset class. By investing a fixed amount at intervals, you buy more mutual fund units when prices are low and fewer when prices are high, helping smooth out market volatility over long horizons.

title: Active Mutual Funds
description: A pooled financial vehicle managed by professional fund managers who actively select assets to outperform the market index.
lockIn: None (except ELSS funds which have 3 years lock-in)
liquidity: High (redeemable daily at prevailing Net Asset Value)
educationalSummary: Active Mutual Funds pool capital from thousands of investors to buy diversified portfolios of stocks or bonds. While they carry higher fees (expense ratios) than index funds, active managers aim to beat market benchmarks through selective investment research.
eligibility: All KYC-compliant domestic and foreign investors

title: Index Funds
description: Passive mutual funds that mirror a market index like Nifty 50 or S&P 500, offering broad market exposure and low cost.
liquidity: High (redeemable daily at prevailing Net Asset Value)
educationalSummary: Index funds aim to replicate index returns rather than beat them. Because they are passively managed, their expense ratios are extremely low. Historically, over long periods (10+ years), low-cost index funds tend to outperform the majority of actively managed equity funds.

title: Gold Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs)
description: Passive investment instruments that track the physical gold price and are traded directly on stock exchanges.
liquidity: Very High (can be sold instantly on stock exchanges during market hours)
educationalSummary: Gold ETFs represent units of physical gold in dematerialized form. Each unit represents approx. 1 gram of 99.5% pure gold. Gold ETFs eliminate risks associated with physical storage, purity issues, and making charges, serving as an excellent inflation hedge.
eligibility: Investors with active Demat and Trading accounts

title: Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGB)
description: Government securities denominated in grams of gold, issued by the RBI as a safe alternative to holding physical gold.
lockIn: 8 years (early exit allowed from 5th year onwards)
liquidity: Moderate (tradable on exchanges, but trading volume can be low)
educationalSummary: SGBs are the ultimate gold investment. Not only do they track gold prices, but the government also pays a guaranteed 2.5% annual interest on the initial investment. Crucially, if held until maturity (8 years), all capital gains are completely exempt from tax.
eligibility: Resident Indian individuals, HUFs, trusts, and universities

title: Physical Gold
description: Investing in physical gold coins, bars, or jewelry, a timeless store of value in Indian households.
liquidity: High (can be sold at any local jeweler or bullion dealer)
educationalSummary: Physical Gold has immense cultural value and offers instant cash liquidity in times of distress. However, it carries high friction costs like making charges (up to 20%), high risk of theft or purity concerns, and lacks regular income yields unlike financial assets.
eligibility: Open to all buyers without restriction

title: Chit Funds
description: A traditional rotating savings and credit system where members contribute monthly and bid for the pooled pot.
lockIn: Duration of the chit cycle (usually 1 to 3 years)
liquidity: Low (subject to monthly bidding cycles and collateral approval)
educationalSummary: Chit funds serve as both a savings tool and a source of emergency micro-loans. While registered chit funds are regulated under the Chit Funds Act, 1982, the sector carries high risk due to unregulated chit scams, defaults by members, or potential promoter fraud.
eligibility: Registered members of certified chit corporations

title: Comprehensive Health Insurance
description: A policy that covers medical, surgical, and hospitalization expenses incurred due to illness or injury.
liquidity: N/A (pays directly for medical claims; no cash value accumulation)
educationalSummary: Health Insurance is a non-negotiable cornerstone of personal finance. A single medical emergency can wipe out years of savings. Health insurance premiums up to ₹25,000 (under age 60) are tax-deductible under Section 80D, protecting both your health and wealth.
eligibility: All individuals (subject to medical underwriting and age entry caps)

title: Term Insurance
description: A pure risk cover life insurance plan that pays a fixed sum to the nominee if the insured dies during the policy term.
lockIn: Duration of policy term (no maturity benefits)
educationalSummary: Term insurance is the cheapest, most efficient way to secure your family's financial future. Unlike hybrid policies (endowment or ULIPs) that combine insurance and investment with poor yields, term insurance keeps premiums low while providing massive coverage (sum assured) to clear liabilities.
eligibility: Typically individuals age 18-65 with stable income sources
